The Aging Parent Financial Organization Checklist

What to list, gather and ask Mom about while there's no rush.

Download PDF

Mom runs her own finances, and nothing about that needs to change. This is a list of what's worth writing down, finding and asking her about, a little at a time and with her say-so. Check what you've done. Anything unchecked is something to get to when it suits you both, not a verdict about Mom or about you.

Gather

Ask Mom about

What this checklist doesn't do

It helps you list, gather and ask. It doesn't say which of these matter for Medicaid planning, what any of them adds up to, or whether anything should change. Rules vary by state, so those questions go to your Medicaid planner or the appropriate licensed professional. Nothing here is legal, financial or tax advice.

Ready for the next step?

You've seen what there is to list, gather and ask Mom about, category by category. The planning interview asks about your family's situation and gives you a free planning report you can bring to any conversation about paying for care.

Where this comes from

Items marked 1 follow AARP's list of records to find and keep in one place. The item marked 2 follows the National Institute on Aging's checklist. The rest come from the Medicaid Planning Roadmap's own working list for this step.
